s.g: Indicates the genitive plural of first-declension and neuter second-declension nouns
to amuse, to give joy, to gladden
Hamburg (a city in, and a state of, Germany)
yokel, bumpkin, hick, redneck (unsophisticated or rural person)
to twitch, to throb, to twinge
keeper of a warehouse or storehouse
monsoon (any of a number of winds associated with regions where most rain falls during a particular season)
to pump, to pressurize, to inflate
to hint (at), to allude, to imply (refer to something indirectly or by suggestion)
to wind around, to wrap around
carriageway (part of a road that carries traffic)
initialism of сего́ числа́ (sevó čislá, “of this date”)
himself/herself/themselves, in the flesh, in person (used to emphasise that someone encountered is a given person)
metropolitan, city (characteristic of urban life in the capital, especially when contrasted with small towns and rural areas)
tokamak (a toroidal chamber in which a plasma is magnetically confined)
to grumble (to make a low growling or rumbling stomach noise)
